**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity).**

- **Clause:** § 7.2 (first of two paragraphs numbered 7.2, p0026) — "Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives."
- **Why it fails:** This is a de facto right of first refusal that restrains our freedom to source elsewhere. It has no product-category limit, no time limit (it runs for the full term), and no automatic termination on Vendor's service-level or delivery failure — so it misses the fallback entirely and lands in walk-away territory. It also contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have given no exclusivity or MFC commitment.
- **Redline (validated, ok:true):** delete p0026, reaching the preferred position (no exclusivity obligation on Customer). The substantive invoicing clause also numbered 7.2 (p0027) is untouched.
- **Not flagged:** the other "exclusive" references (§§ 13.1, 14.2, 19.4, 21.4, 28.1–28.2, 30.2) go to licence scope, remedies and jurisdiction, not exclusive dealing; § 12.3 benefits us. Treated as a sourcing restraint rather than double-flagging the MFN pricing limb.
